claims.text: The initial material is cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr.
Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility.
Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C and strain rates of 10^-4–10^-2 s^-1.
Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has poor oxygen resistance.
A thin, uniform aluminide coating can be applied by pack cementation or atomic layer deposition.
The aluminide coating will convert into a stable, adherent Al2O3 scale during high-temperature exposure.
The resulting Al2O3 scale will be continuous and adherent.
The Al2O3 scale will act as a diffusion barrier to oxygen.
Blocking oxygen ingress will significantly reduce oxidation of HfNbTaTiZr.
The coating will not alter the underlying alloy microstructure that governs mechanical properties.
At 1000 °C in air for about 100 hours, coated specimens will have lower oxidation weight gain than untreated specimens.
At 1000 °C in air for about 100 hours, coated specimens will develop a thinner oxide scale than untreated specimens.
After coating and oxidation exposure, room-temperature tensile ductility will remain within 8–16%.
After coating and oxidation exposure, yield strength at 1000 °C and strain rates of 10^-4–10^-2 s^-1 will remain within 163–530 MPa.
The proposed operating boundary is approximately 1000 °C in air for about 100 hours.
The proposed mechanical-testing boundary is a strain-rate range of 10^-4–10^-2 s^-1.
Long-term alumina-scale adhesion and integrity under cyclic thermal-mechanical loading are uncertain.
Possible effects of the coating process on the near-surface microstructure are uncertain.

contradictions.description: The conditions imply mechanical loading during the 100-hour oxidation exposure, whereas the experimental design specifies oxidation first and tensile testing afterward.
